clue.text: Thus little boy creates disgust

parts.note: sic is the Latin word for thus, used in quotations
Ken is a short boy's name, a little form of Kenneth

explanation.surface: A small child's behaviour turns someone's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone feel ill or revolted is the transitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: High charge increased, among a variety of extras

indicators.note: among says the word for increased sits inside the shuffled letters
a variety of suggests the letters of extras come in a varied order

parts.note: prices that have increased have gone up

explanation.surface: A fee has gone up and is lumped in with lots of other add-ons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High charge' reads as a big fee; it is a top-rate income levy. 'a variety of' shuffles the extras and 'among' sets the rise inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional levy on high incomes is a steep tax, so a heavy charge.

clue.text: A romance developed around Northern Irish region

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters surround the abbreviation
developed suggests the letters have grown into a new shape, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A love affair blossomed in the north of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges A ROMANCE to CONEMARA, and 'around' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Connemara is a district in County Galway in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Origins of Europe mentioned in this broadcast

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Where things in Europe start is noted in this transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: To send out a signal or sound is to transmit it, a verb sense of broadcast.

clue.text: Terrapin's not a terribly fast mover

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled, an anagram signal

parts.note: the possessive is read as terrapin is, so its final S joins the letters to be rearranged
the letter a is the part removed from the anagram fodder, which the word not signals

explanation.surface: A turtle is hardly a speedy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges TERRAPINS; the answer's letters plus A make that word, so 'not a' takes A away.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete or animal built for short bursts of speed runs quickly over short distances.

clue.text: School place is secured, it's assumed

indicators.note: the place is secured, held inside, by the word for school

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: Getting into a school is taken for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: School here is a group of whales, POD, which holds SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put forward as true without proof has been supposed or postulated.

clue.text: Snooker player may be wanted by the police?

explanation.surface: A snooker champion is suspected of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A snooker game is played in frames, so a player at the table is literally inside one; the idiom also means being a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is competing in the current game of snooker; the idiom also means under suspicion, a suspect sought by detectives.

clue.text: Take top off solid piece of furniture

indicators.note: taking the top off a word in a down clue removes its first letter

parts.note: something solid and steady is stable

explanation.surface: Lift the lid from a sturdy item in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped piece with legs for eating or working at is household furnishing.

clue.text: Gives response concerning elements of play

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: Someone answers questions about parts of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who responds to a stimulus behaves in answer to it.

clue.text: Respectable characters in trade centre

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, inside the phrase trade centre spell the answer

explanation.surface: Upstanding people are found in a commercial hub.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proper and of good standing behaves in an acceptable, honest manner.

clue.text: Poor writer takes river boat

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
the Nile is the great African river
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An impoverished author goes on a river cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all means being broke, utterly impoverished.

clue.text: I closed my teeth around a bone

indicators.note: around signals turning the phrase round so it reads backwards

parts.note: if I closed my teeth on something, I bit it

explanation.surface: Someone bit down hard on a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns I BIT round to TIBI, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone is the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Regretted have governed without centre left

indicators.note: without centre means the middle letter is removed, here the one standing for left

parts.note: to have governed is to have ruled

explanation.surface: A former leader is sorry they ruled without the moderate left.
explanation.walkthrough: The L removed is the middle letter of RULED, which is why 'centre' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt sorrow over something done is the past of the verb meaning to repent.

clue.text: Colony's agreement

explanation.surface: A colonial outpost reaches a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A new community founded by incomers is a colony; a resolved dispute ends in a deal or accord.

clue.text: Hoot, catching a boy dressing

indicators.note: catching means the word for hoot grabs the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a hoot is something hilarious, as is a scream
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A howl as a lad is caught putting on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoot here is a very funny thing, SCREAM, not an owl's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy condiment poured over leaves is a salad topping, a kind of dressing.

clue.text: Firm churned out data about worker

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the worker
churned out suggests the letters are stirred up, an anagram signal

parts.note: to man a post is to work it, and a man is a worker

explanation.surface: A company spews out figures on an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective. 'churned out' shuffles the data and 'about' wraps it round the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshakeable and resolute describes someone who will not change their mind.

clue.text: Frank's aim

explanation.surface: A man named Frank has a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means straightforward and candid; to aim means to point or steer something at a target.

clue.text: On watch in disorderly part of San Francisco, perhaps

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police keep an eye on a rowdy district of a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cities have an ethnic Chinese quarter, San Francisco's being famous, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Inexperienced players not finishing drink

parts.note: someone new and naive is green

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: New players leave before the end to have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves make a light infusion popular in Asia.

clue.text: Old man's given chopped vegetable and fruit

parts.note: old man is slang for father, papa, with 's meaning has

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a yam is a starchy root vegetable

explanation.surface: Dad has been handed diced veg and some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Old man's' is 'has', joining papa to the cut-down yam.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawpaw is a tropical orange-fleshed fruit.

clue.text: Leave a group of people working

parts.note: a band is a group of people
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Quit a team that's still busy.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or forsake someone is to go away and leave them behind.

clue.text: With bounder about, one's more nervous

indicators.note: about means the word for bounder goes around the letter for one

parts.note: a jumper bounds, a jumper is a bounder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: With a cad hanging around, someone gets jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bounder' is usually a cad; here it is anything that bounds, a JUMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jittery and easily startled describes someone edgy, the comparative form.

clue.text: Famous singer's car (German)

parts.note: Jag is short for a Jaguar car

explanation.surface: A celebrated vocalist drives a German motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick of the Rolling Stones is a renowned rock vocalist.

clue.text: Artist raised objections over total rubbish

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
BS is short for bullshit, total rubbish

explanation.surface: A painter has complained about utter garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUTS upwards into STUB. George Stubbs was an English painter famous for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an eighteenth-century English painter of horses.

clue.text: Accept person in care is to rule the roost

parts.note: to take is to accept
a charge is someone placed in another's care

explanation.surface: Agreeing to look after someone makes you the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume control is to be in command, the idiom for being boss.

clue.text: Executioner's vessel

explanation.surface: The hangman owns a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English hangman whose surname became slang for an executioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was an infamous English hangman; a two-masted sailing boat is also so named.

clue.text: Mist in Middlesex location, we've heard

indicators.note: we've heard signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: Hayes is a town in the old county of Middlesex, west London

explanation.surface: Fog hangs over a London suburb, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: MIDDLESEX is a former English county now mostly in Greater London.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin fog or vapour blurring the air is a light mist.

clue.text: Wine that, in test, is tastiest

indicators.note: the clue says the wine put in the word test makes tastiest, so test is removed from tastiest

parts.note: the wine is set inside the word test to make this word, not read as a run of its letters, so its appearance here is a coincidence of the construction

explanation.surface: The wine that, in a blind tasting, is judged best.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tasting verdict, but it says the wine slipped into 'test' makes 'tastiest', so 'in' tells you to remove one word from the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white from Piedmont.

clue.text: Go swimming with male at club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man takes a dip at his sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a dip in the sea or a pool is to swim.

clue.text: Fashion code, with stars in formal wear

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A dress code for celebrities requires evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb here, rearranging CODE and STARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat worn for evening occasions is a man's formal garment.

clue.text: School fellow entertained by a French or German musician

indicators.note: entertained by means the fellow is held inside the French word

parts.note: un is French for a
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A classmate is hosted by a French or German composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: After struggle, Napoleon gutted a European capital

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Napoleon was devastated after a fight in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: Gutted NAPOLEON leaves its first and last letters, N and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria's capital city sits on the Danube.
